title: The US economy added just 29,000 jobs last month and the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% | CNN Business
text:
Source: CNN

Job growth was slower than expected in September, as the US economy added just 29,000 jobs last month and the unemployment rate increased to 4.2%, new Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed Friday.

September’s job gains marked a slowdown from August, when a downwardly revised 133,000 jobs were added. But economists cautioned that August’s surprisingly strong gain likely reflected some seasonal factors that overstated hiring activity.

Employers were expected to add about 90,000 jobs in September with an unemployment rate holding at 4.1%.

Recent months’ job growth was slower than expected as July and August’s employment estimates were revised down by a combined 60,000 jobs. Following revisions, there was an estimated 133,000 jobs added in August (previously 162,000) and July turned negative, with 10,000 jobs lost in July (previously a 21,000-job gain).

Through September, the economy has added an average of 68,000 jobs per month, BLS data shows. Employment gains have picked up from last year, which was one of the weakest on record (with below 10,000 jobs added per month). However, the current pace of hiring is running well below pre-pandemic averages (120,000 jobs per month).

The job market has mostly been holding up despite a growing list of threats to hiring, from an aging population and the rapid adoption of AI to higher oil prices, policy uncertainty and the war with Iran.

This story is developing and will be updated.
